text: Standing privileged access is exposed all day for a benefit it only needs for a fraction of that time. Just-in-time access removes that exposure directly: a user requests elevation only when they actually need it, instead of holding a privileged role continuously.

The request gets approved — sometimes automatically, sometimes requiring a second person's sign-off — and the role activates for a defined, limited window: an hour, four hours, whatever the task genuinely requires. Then it's automatically revoked when that window closes, with nobody needing to remember to remove it afterward.

Azure PIM is the concrete mechanism behind this in Entra ID. An admin made eligible for Global Administrator doesn't hold it day to day. To use it, they activate the role with a justification and often an MFA challenge, sometimes waiting on an approver, and PIM grants it for a few hours before automatically deactivating it and logging the whole event.

JIT handles privileged roles well, but most access — file shares, application roles, group memberships — is granted once and just persists. Access reviews are the discipline for that: on a schedule, typically quarterly, the actual manager or resource owner looks at who has access and explicitly confirms whether it's still needed.

That's deliberate — a central IT team reviewing a list in isolation usually can't tell whether a given employee still needs access to a given finance system, but that employee's manager usually can. Anything not affirmatively confirmed during the review gets revoked, not left in place by default.

Without either discipline, access creep is the default outcome: people change teams and keep old access, temporary coverage for a colleague never gets revoked, project permissions just stay after the project ends. None of that is malicious — it's what happens, reliably, with no recurring mechanism forcing a second look. From here, the course moves from these authorization models into Windows system hardening, starting with building a GPO baseline from a real benchmark.
